verdict.line: You lose if you eat Parrrley poke for free through levels 1-5, you win if you survive to 6 and start landing Feast kills.

brief.thesis: Gangplank wins the poke war at range 625 before level 6 but has no way to escape or punish Cho'Gath once Rupture-Feast threatens a kill. The data backs this: Gangplank has the lane advantage, but Cho'Gath holds the solo-kill edge and a 54.6% head-to-head win rate over 302 games because the lane flips hard once R (Feast) comes online.

theirWindow.when: before level 6, you're in Q range
theirWindow.what: Gangplank freely lands Q (Parrrley, 5s cooldown, 625 range) into auto-attack poison stacks while you have no way to close the gap. Play off CS, don't walk up to trade until you have minion cover for Rupture.

yourWindow.what: Hit W (Feral Scream, 13s cooldown, 300 range cone) to silence so he can't Remove Scurvy the slow, then Q (Rupture, 9s cooldown, 950 range) to knock up and slow, then walk in and R (Feast, 60s cooldown, 175 range) for true damage. If it kills, you gain a permanent max-HP stack.

start.why: 25.5% pick rate at 56.8% win over 95 games; the flat damage reduction blunts Parrrley poke and poison ticks so you can actually hold CS without burning potions early.

boots.why: 50.3% pick at 53.9% win over 178 games; Gangplank's damage is auto-attack and poison based, so the flat physical reduction directly cuts his poke and sustained trades.

core.why: The dash is your answer to his kiting - it closes the gap he built with Parrrley so your Feast window at level 6+ actually connects.

situational.when: he's building toward raw poke damage and you need more sustain to hold lane
his team is stacking crit or attack speed and you need the active slow to stick your Rupture engages
the game is going long and you want a bigger HP stat-check instead of the Rocketbelt dash pattern

runes.keystoneWhy: The burst of extra attacks lets you win the all-in the moment you land Rupture + Feral Scream silence, converting your level-6 window into a kill before he can Remove Scurvy anything other than the hard CC.

summoners.why: 56.6% win at 64.5% pick rate; Teleport lets you reset after losing the early poke war without bleeding CS, and you don't need Ignite since your all-in already comes from true damage on R, not burst.

playing.title: Farm under tower pre-6
playing.detail: Don't contest trades level 1-5; Vorpal Spikes (E) only triggers on your attacks, so last-hitting from max range still ticks it while you absorb poke with Doran's Shield.

playing.title: Track his Remove Scurvy cooldown
playing.detail: W (Remove Scurvy, 22/21/20/19/18s cooldown) clears your Rupture slow and silence if he's used it recently. Bait it out with a Q poke before committing your real all-in.

playing.title: Silence before you commit
playing.detail: Land W (Feral Scream) first in your level-6 engage - the silence stops him from using Remove Scurvy to cleanse your Rupture knockup/slow mid-fight.

playing.title: Save Feast for the kill, not poke
playing.detail: R (Feast, 60s cooldown) only grows you if it kills. Don't throw it into a trade unless you're certain of the kill or you lose the stack opportunity for 60 seconds.

playing.title: Respect Cannon Barrage after 6
playing.detail: His ultimate (120/115/110/120/120s cooldown, global range) can zone you off a push or punish a bad base timer. Watch his ult icon before committing to extended sieges.

playing.title: Rocketbelt removes his kiting advantage
playing.detail: Once you have the dash, his only tool to disengage is Remove Scurvy's heal, not distance. Force fights near level 9-10 once the item is online.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, and summoners are pulled directly from measured games on the current patch (16.20.1); the power-curve timing and trade-pattern reasoning is my own read of the kit interactions.

stats.opponentTip: Avoid being hit by Gangplank’s Grasp of the Undying – (Q). Keep your distance while focusing on farming and contesting lane while waiting for a chance after reaching level 6.
